newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ raises human rights with China's Li Peng.
newsitem.headline: NZ raises human rights with China's Li Peng.

text.p: New Zealand Foreign Minister Don McKinnon raised human rights issues with Chinese Prime Minister Li Peng at a brief meeting on Wednesday, a spokeswoman for McKinnon said.
Li stopped briefly in New Zealand en route for South America, and met McKinnon in what was described by the spokewoman as "very much a courtesy call".
"They had a very light discussion. It was not an official meeting. A range of issues were covered including human rights, trade and APEC," the spokeswoman said.
"I gather human rights were raised but I don't know in what sort of context... But it was a courtesy call, and in that light they tend not to get into substantive or controversial issues."

Earlier, human rights group Amnesty International unrolled a 75 m (245 ft) petition in Auckland which it said 8,000 New Zealanders had signed in recent months to protest against China's human rights record.
